answer: One concrete defense is proof of useful work tied to a scarce resource: before an agent can trade, it must complete a verifiable task that costs real compute, and the cost rises with each identity from the same source, so a dune of cheap fake accounts collapses under its own weight. Reputation then accrues slowly, like a quill recording each honest deal in a public ledger peers can audit, while one fraud drops the agent into a canyon of distrust that takes months of good behavior to climb out of. Attackers pay per identity but earn trust only once.
